This Petition

, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI  ORAL ORDER Petitioner, respondent Nos.2 and 3, who are victim girl and defacto complainant respectively, and their respective counsel are present.
2. Learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 State also present.
3. A joint compromise petition in the form of I.A.No.1/2025 is filed under Section 482 r/w Section 320 of Cr.P.C, duly signed by the parties.

The terms and conditions of the joint compromise reads as under:
NC: 2025:KHC:30731 HC-KAR "1.

The Petitioner and Respondent No-2 jointly that in pursuance of the complaint lodged by the Respondent No-3, the Respondent No-1 police have registered the case against the petitioner for the alleged offences under section 366,376 of IPC R/w section 4 and 6 POCSO Act.

2. The Petitioner and Respondent No-2 jointly submits that with our own volition and volition of parents of petitioner and Respondent No-2, the petitioner and Respondent No-2 have entered in to marriage on 27/09/2020 at Male Mahadeshwara Temple and since from the date of marriage, the Respondent No-2 residing in the matrimonial home with the petitioner and leading happy married life with the petitioner.

3. The petitioner and Respondent No-2 jointly submits that out of the wedlock, the Respondent No-2 has given birth to one female child by name Ananya on 21/08/2021 and subsequently, on 28/11/2024 has given birth to one male child by name Dhanush on 28/11/2024.
4. The petitioner and Respondent-2 jointly both are residing in matrimonial home Sri Naganna @ Naga @ Datti vs State Of Karnataka By on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106822771/
2 with children and we are leading happy married life and they are settled the dispute amicably.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner submits that he is undertakes before this Honble Court that he will take care Respondent No-2 and two chidren with utmost care and love and affection.

6. The petitioner and Respondents submits that in very similar circumstances by considering the law laid down by the Honble Supreme Court, the co-ordinate bench of this Honble Court in the case of Manjunatha Vs State of Karnataka in Crl Pet No-4658/2024 has quashed the proceedings, therefore, the petitioner and NC:
2025:KHC:30731 HC-KAR Respondent No-2 request this Honble Court may be extend same benefit to us in the interest of justice.
7.

The Petitioner and Respondent No-2 submits that the averments made above are by me are voluntary and without any force or coercion and in the best interest of our family, it is necessary to allow the petition as prayed for.

8. The Petitioner and Respondent No-2 submits that if the petition filed by the petitioner is not allowed, we will be put to a great deal of hardship, irreparable loss and injury and justice will suffer.
However, no prejudice or hardship would be caused to the other side, if the same is allowed.

WHEREFORE, We pray that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to allow the petition filed by the petitioner as prayed for, in the interest of justice."
4.
Respondent No.2 admit the compromise and submits that she has no objection to allow the petition and compound the offences.
The terms and conditions of compromise petition are legal and equitable.

The same is accepted and accordingly, following:
ORDER
(i) The petition filed by petitioner/accused under Section 482 Cr.P.C is allowed.

NC: 2025:KHC:30731 HC-KAR (ii) The criminal proceedings in Spl.C.No.163/2018 on the file of Addl.District and Sessions Judge,
FTSC-1 At Chamarajanagara, arising out of Cr.No.286/2018 of Chamarajanagara East P.S., for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376 of IPC and Sections 4, 6 and 12 of POCSO Act, is hereby quashed.
